title: [@inlined] on a function with an optional argument is not honoured and gets no warning
summary: `(f [@inlined]) ~x:1 y`, for an exported `f` with an optional argument with a default, inlines only the wrapper that fills in the default; the call of the function proper stays, with no warning 55. At `-O2` or with `-stubs-forward-inlining` it is inlined.
commands: awk '/^caml.*:$/ {p = /^camlTest__caller/; n = 0} p && /(call|jmp).*f_inner/ {n++} p && /@function/ {print "calls of f_inner in caller:", n}' test.s

expected.text: `f` is inlined in `caller` (or warning 55): prints `calls of f_inner in caller: 0`.

actual.text: No warning; prints `calls of f_inner in caller: 1`.

cause: `lambda/simplif.ml`, `split_default_wrapper`: the wrapper's call of `f_inner` carries the default inlining attribute, not the caller's, unless `-stubs-forward-inlining` is given.
reference: related: issue #7724, PR #6037 (adds -stubs-forward-inlining, off by default)
